chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): In

a woman who lost her husband or was notified of his death, so she married, then her husband returned after that and divorced her. He said: 'She observes the waiting period for both of them together, three months, as one single waiting period, and the latter [husband] cannot marry her ever.'

key_terms.نُعِيَ إِلَيْهَا: notification of death was conveyed to her

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period and marital status for a woman whose first husband returns after she married a second man due to his presumed death?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling of *Iddah al-Mutah* (waiting period for remarriage) in cases of *Ghayb* (presumed death), establishing that the woman observes a single three-month period for both the first and second marriages. Crucially, it distinguishes this scenario from *Iddah al-Talaq* by ruling that the second husband is permanently prohibited (*Mahram*) from marrying her, unlike the temporary prohibition in standard divorce cases. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for resolving complexities arising from the uncertainty of a spouse's status during the *Iddah* period.
